answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: adaptive registration difficulty that scales with correlated signups. Each new identity solves a proof-of-work puzzle whose cost rises as more accounts share one origin fingerprint, like a copper coil heating with current. Model signups as an atlas of vertices; when many cluster at a single origin vertex, difficulty for that cluster climbs steeply. One honest agent pays little, but an attacker minting a thousand correlated fakes faces super-linear cost, since each clone raises the price of the next, so flooding grows punishing fast, not merely linear.
